description: We are Universo Diario. In this challenge, we will tell the story of the equipment NASA left on the Moon, Mars, and beyond. Our goal is to create a scientific storytelling project (PDF and Website) that teaches young people about both the hardware and the astrophysics discoveries made possible by those instruments, using real information and images from NASA & other Space Agencies.
summary: Me Jose David Ortiz Useche & Charles Nicolas Prader created a website that can be used for the people of all ages to learn about the Mechanism / equipment used by NASA into the Moon and Mars, it adresses the challenge because we were asked to create something useful for the people to learn about all the "Abandoned but not Forgotten" things that the NASA & other Space Agencies created in order for the evolution and knowledge of humanity, it is important because it helps us to learn about new things, to learn about the devices that gived us all the information that we have and we use for our experiments in today's date.
details:
Abandoned but not Forgotten is a website by Universo Diario that tells the stories of the equipment NASA has left on the Moon, on Mars, and beyond. Visitors start on a Home page with a video banner and featured story links, then open the Readings library of eight stories (Pioneer 10, InSight, Mars Pathfinder and Sojourner, the Apollo Lunar Module, the Lunar Roving Vehicle, Viking 1, Kepler, and Ingenuity). Each one explains what the spacecraft was built to do, what it discovered, and how it shaped later missions, using real information and images from NASA and the NSSDCA, with sources credited.

The project turns complex space hardware and astrophysics discoveries into short, readable stories for people, with the goal of inspiring curiosity about space science and engineering and showing that these instruments still teach us about other worlds even after their missions have ended. We built the site with Wix and its Wix.AI features and used Grok AI to help with research and editing. It is creative because it uses storytelling instead of a data catalog, presenting each “abandoned but not forgotten” mission as a character with a beginning, a challenge, and a lasting legacy, supported by a video banner and a browsable story gallery. We considered scientific accuracy by relying on NASA sources, an audience of young learners, simple navigation (Home, About, Contact, Readings), and a public site that anyone can open without signing in.
